qualificationScope: Recorded fixture profiles only; target_capabilities observes availability but does not certify arbitrary targets.
featureIdPolicy: Exact public MCP name, change.<kind>, or a stable explicit backlog ID.

criteria.requirement: Resolve exact target identity and reject ambiguous, inconsistent or stale selectors.
Distinguish empty results from inaccessible, truncated, unsupported or unobserved scope.
Preserve unrelated native program content and metadata; no-change roundtrips are semantically unchanged.
Require matching previews, conflict checks and explicit intended object scope before mutation.
Native compile/readback and save/reopen checks pass for the specified fixture; compile alone is not behavior proof.
Retain verifiable checkpoint/outcome after partial failure and demonstrate recovery without replaying uncertain writes.
Assert independently specified stimulus/expected behavior on an identified running simulated program; no blocked/skipped run is a pass.
Record environment, target, operation, outcome, artifacts and limitations; never promote fixtures to universal support.
Confirm native simulator inventory, ownership, instance lifecycle or observed CPU state for the specific operation; no program behavior claim.
Verify the owned offline simulation destination, compile result, protected credential handling and generated virtual card; no running-program claim.

features.title: Apply a PLC library integration plan as one change

reasons: Reuses the existing library_instantiate and graphical_typed_edit routes (PlcBlockComposition.CreateFrom, PlcBlockComposition.Import, Project.Save/Archive, ICompilable.Compile, LibraryTypeVersion.FindInstances/Export); no new Siemens API.

limitations: Natively qualified as a production route on owned de-DE-only scratch projects with CPU 1511-1 PN (V21) for the captured FB/UDT component, a new or existing FBD FC caller and a new global instance DB (local.library_integrate.combined_apply.20261028).

Off by default. Only a Host started with --enable-library-integrate-apply executes a prepared PLC library_integrate plan in change_apply; other Hosts refuse it with PlcIntegrationNotQualified exactly as before. With the flag, the preview states eligibility in combinedApply.

Runs only the verified shapes: fresh FB/dependency import from a read-only global library source with its retained snapshot, a new global instance DB, a new FBD FC caller or an existing one inserting after its last network in the standard PLC scope, root scalar tag bindings, no planner blockers or planOnly steps. OB insertion is refused; LAD and FB callers, earlier placements in an existing caller, reuse, multi-instances, software units, HMI targets and PLC/HMI recipes stay plan-only and refuse with PlcIntegrationNotQualified.

The plan previewHash, library fingerprint and source hashes are rechecked under one admitted exclusive lease before the idempotency claim. Each step is freshly prepared, bound to the reviewed plan, applied with compile and save, and verified by readback (import identity/content, caller insertion and instance DB). Steps are not atomic.

The import step's complete-project archive, taken before the first mutation, is the change's single recovery checkpoint. Any failure stops at that step, records failedStep and leaves recovery_required; change_restore on the change retrieves the checkpoint into a new location in an empty owned Portal and never replays a step. Automatic in-place rollback is not available.

The new instance DB uses the natively captured storage profile when the installed FB/UDT content equals the captured component (de-DE only), otherwise the shipped typed instance templates; a callee neither covers refuses at fresh typed preparation with InstanceCreationProfileUnavailable.

reasons: Requires --enable-library-integrate-apply. Normal Hosts keep PLC library_integrate plan-only.

Unified external_tag_create (26 October): exact same-HMI connection and root PLC tag identities; prepare proves the PLC owner from native CommunicationManagement endpoints and the exact scalar type, apply sets Connection then PlcTag and verifies the natively derived name/type/symbolic access/PLC name. The prepare-only native probe passed on Unified Comfort (local.hmi.external-tag-prepare.20261026): owner/tag/type proof reached the closed gate and name, type and foreign-PLC requests were refused. Apply stays behind the closed Unified preservation gate and is unqualified; Unified PC, arrays, whole UDT values, software-unit tags and Classic external tags are not covered; global DB members and connection creation follow (27 October).

Unified HMI writes beyond screens (27 October): external_tag_create also accepts an exact root global DB identity (kind block) plus an unquoted memberPath; prepare exports the DB and requires exactly one declared member with no array on its path and an exactly matching scalar type, then writes the natively observed dotted spelling (DB.Member, as in the HmiSeeder LinkedDbValue fixture). Struct/UDT sub-members qualify only when the DB export declares them; arrays, quoted or indexed names, instance/array DBs and software-unit DBs are refused. connection_create (target the HMI as kind hmiDevice) calls HmiSoftware.Connections.Create(name) only when exactly one valid native CommunicationManagement HMI endpoint pair of that LocalConnectionName has exactly one partner PLC; Partner/Station/Node are read-only in V21, so apply requires the readback Partner to equal the proven PLC software name and a nonempty CommunicationDriver. Whether Create derives the partner from an existing endpoint pair (or the HMI already lists that connection) is unobserved; the Partner-to-PLC-name mapping is an assumption that fails closed. object_create (DiscreteAlarms, AnalogAlarms, DataLogs, AlarmLogs) uses the composition's Create(name) and object_properties_set edits an exact alarm (hmiAlarm), log or runtime settings (hmiModelNode at its hmi_inspect section=model path); both use per-family allowlists of documented typed setters (alarms: RaisedStateTag, RaisedStateTagBitNumber, TriggerMode, Condition, AlarmClass, Priority, Origin, Area; logs: Settings.LogMaxSize, Settings.StorageFolder; runtime settings: StartScreen, ScreenResolution) with exact typed readback, and require RaisedStateTag, AlarmClass and StartScreen to name an existing tag, alarm class or top-level screen of the same HMI. features.title: Prepare reviewed offline force-table document edits

reasons: V21 PublicAPI P:Siemens.Engineering.SW.WatchAndForceTables.PlcWatchAndForceTableGroup.ForceTables, M:Siemens.Engineering.SW.WatchAndForceTables.PlcForceTableComposition.Import(System.IO.FileInfo,Siemens.Engineering.ImportOptions) with ImportOptions.Override, M:Siemens.Engineering.SW.WatchAndForceTables.PlcForceTable.Export(System.IO.FileInfo,Siemens.Engineering.ExportOptions) with WithDefaults, P:Siemens.Engineering.SW.WatchAndForceTables.PlcForceTable.Entries/IsConsistent/Name and read-only P:Siemens.Engineering.SW.WatchAndForceTables.PlcForceTableEntry.Name/Address/DisplayFormat/ForceValue/ForceIntention; durable checkpoint/journal state is a Host service, not a vendor transaction.

Installed metadata has no setter on any PlcForceTableEntry property or on PlcForceTable.Name, and no force-table Create or Delete, so entries change only through the reviewed exported document and Import(Override). The installed metadata does not state that a PLC has exactly one force table; the manual does.

limitations: 2026-10-27: watch_table_prepare with forceTable=true edits the existing force table document through the watch preserving editor: field (Name, Address, DisplayFormat, ForceValue), comment (existing culture), clone, delete and reorder, one reviewed edit per operation. Only fields already present as plain text in the captured export can be set; no row grammar is synthesized.

ForceIntention is never set. A captured or imported force table with any typed or serialized ForceIntention other than false refuses preparation, import and save. Nothing is forced, monitored or written online.

Typed/XML readback compares a field the export omits as empty, so rows with omitted fields (for example an Undef display format) are refused until a native profile settles the omission rules. Document ID reindexing is not offered for force rows.

Force-table create, rename and delete are not offered (no V21 API). The planner-backed watch_table_prepare_authoring route stays watch-only: it materializes FB-instance watch rows with ModifyValue, which do not fit force rows.

Access rules are exposed only through the DeviceItem service Siemens.Engineering.HW.Features.WatchAndForceTableAccessManager (ForcetableAccessRules, ForceTableAccessRuleComposition.Create/Find, ForceTableAccessRule.Access/Delete), not on PlcForceTable. They are hardware web/display configuration, are not edited here and stay in the peer manifest, so an import that drops a rule fails preservation.

Worker-owned saved offline scratch only. Production Hosts dispatch the natively qualified force edits; reorder and the Name field stay with the isolated qualification harness, like the other expanded document edits.

Native (29 October 2026, local.watch.force-edits.20261029): on rows an operator authored in the TIA editor, the ForceValue, Address and DisplayFormat field edits, comment, clone and delete pass with checkpoint, readback, unchanged peers, fresh reopen and checkpoint restore. Reorder is refused at readback, because TIA renumbers the rows' document IDs, and is recovered. The Name field is not exercised. watch_table_reconcile_interrupted is qualified on watch tables (local.watch.native.20261028), not on a force table.

Edits the force table document only; it never forces. V21 Openness, the PLCSIM Advanced V8 Runtime API, the S7-1500 Web API and OPC UA expose no force route (docs/plans/live-monitoring-forcing-plan.md); forcing stays a TIA Portal UI action.

reasons: Production Hosts dispatch the natively qualified force edits (ForceValue, Address and DisplayFormat fields, comment, clone, delete; maintainer decision of 29 October 2026). Reorder and the Name field require --component-qualification and --watch-qualification.

Generated FB step/transition structures (G7_StepPlus_V6/G7_TransitionPlus_V6) are renamed or removed with their element; none is synthesized for added elements, whose empty LAD supervision/interlock modules use the recorded seed shape. limitations: Natively qualified on one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN (V21) (local.access.qualify.20261028): the public DER of a certificate this run created and deleted; PEM, CA-issued and foreign certificates are not imported natively.

Payload: hardwarePath, uploadRef (committed artifact upload) and format der or pem. The Host turns the upload into exact public DER (PublicCertificateReview.PublicDer): exactly one certificate; PKCS#12/PFX, PKCS#7, private or encrypted keys, surplus data and any other payload field, including a password, refuse. Generic uploads retain their bytes before this check.
The worker re-checks the DER, imports a hash-pinned change artifact and verifies exactly one new certificate without a private key whose exported public DER has the reviewed SHA-256.
Importing does not establish trust, usage or assignment. Refused while EnableGlobalCertificatesStore is true; V21 exposes neither the project-wide store nor a store migration.

Previews, readbacks and journals carry public identity only (SHA-256 of the exported DER, subject, issuer, validity, alternative names, store); private-key presence is a flag and private keys are never read, exported or accepted. Checkpoint restore recovers the project, not proven private-key recoverability, and changes no device or client trust.

features.title: Set the CPU system web page flag and default web application from exact expected values

reasons: V21 public API: HW.Features.SystemWebPagesFeature.EnableSystemWebPages (settable), DefaultWebPagesFeature.WebApplicationConfigurations, WebApplicationConfiguration.IsDefault (settable), Name, ApplicationType; DeviceItem.GetAttribute("WebserverActivate").

limitations: Natively qualified on one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN (V21) (local.access.qualify.20261028): webServerActive on and off and systemWebPages on the scratch CPU; defaultApplication is only refused, never written.

Payload: webServerActive {expected, value} (the CPU's Boolean WebserverActivate attribute, only where it is writable), systemWebPages {expected, value} and/or defaultApplication {expected, value} with an application name or null for none. expected must equal the current value at prepare (StaleRevision otherwise); any other field is refused.

compile=true is mandatory and compiles all project devices. The change fingerprint adds every web-capable CPU's WebserverActivate value and page settings; interruption reconciliation holds the outcome for review.

features.title: Set the CPU OPC UA server state, port, certificate acceptance and purchased runtime license from exact expected values

reasons: V21 public API: DeviceItem.GetAttribute/SetAttribute on the CPU's OPC UA sub-item (OpcUaServer; while the server is on also OpcUaPort and OpcUaAutoAcceptAllClientCertificates) and on the CPU (OpcUaPurchasedLicense, UInt64 0..3 NoLicense/SimaticOpcUaS71500Small/Medium/Large per the V21 hardware parameter description). Names pinned from native captures on CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 (fixtures/opcua/server-settings-v21-1511-v41.json).

limitations: Natively qualified on one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 (V21 Update 3) (local.opcua.server-settings.20261028): activation with the Small license, port and automatic certificate acceptance, each with checkpoint, device compile, save, native readback, fresh-Portal reopen, and change_restore of the activation to the exact attribute state.

Payload fields serverEnabled, port (1..65535), autoAcceptClientCertificates, runtimeLicense and guestAccess, each optional and each { expected, value }; expected must equal the current native value at prepare (ExpectedValueMismatch otherwise). Any other field is refused; passwords, certificates and users are never accepted.

port and autoAcceptClientCertificates exist natively only while the server is on, so they are set in a later change than the activation; otherwise UnsupportedCapability. guestAccess is always refused: V21 models guest access as the UMAC anonymous user holding the OPCUAServerAccess device right, which neither this kind nor umac_role_set changes.

V21 refuses to compile an active OPC UA server unless a user holds the OPCUAServerAccess device right; grant it first with umac_role_set. Enabling the server makes TIA assign a server certificate at compile.
runtimeLicense records the purchased license in the project; it neither verifies nor activates an entitlement.

Apply writes serverEnabled first when enabling and last when disabling, then reads every requested attribute back. compile=true is mandatory and compiles all project devices. The change fingerprint adds every device item's pinned OPC UA server attribute values; interruption reconciliation holds the outcome for review.
Offline project settings only: nothing is downloaded, and clients, server certificates and endpoint reachability are not checked.
